findings.summary: Durable source-job claim path is not compare-and-set fenced before work.
findings.details: The task requires sourceProcessingJobs leases/CAS with claim-by-compare-and-set, opaque lease token, owner, expiry, attempt, heartbeat, reclaim, and stale-worker completion fencing. The actual workpool handler enqueues an action first and only calls startSourceJob inside onComplete after the action has finished, then blindly patches the row from the row snapshot. That leaves the external/background work outside the durable lease and CAS contract.

packages/convex/confect/jobs/workpool.ts:183-214 claims, records response, and succeeds only in onComplete after work completion.

findings.summary: Required crash/failure matrix is not proved against durable handlers.
findings.details: The focused tests exercise pure reducer helpers and source-code string containment, but do not execute the Convex workpool/sourceProcessingJobs handlers for crash before/after claim, after external response, before/after commit, before ACK, or duplicate external-call versus one accepted effect. The implemented handler also combines response receipt and commit in one mutation path, so the required persisted recovery points are not demonstrably present.

findings.summary: Declared failure contract is not surfaced or reachable through the Confect/Convex API.
findings.details: The task requires typed errors LeaseLost, RetryableJobFailure, PermanentJobFailure, MaxAttemptsReached, StaleGeneration, and DuplicateEffect. The Confect spec does not declare expected errors, the public/internal functions return work IDs, component status, or null, and the handler swallows reducer Left values by returning null. Retryable, permanent, cancellation, revoked, and superseded states are reducer-only and not reachable from the registered workpool functions.
